summary: Weddly backend smoke-tested via external REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL using MongoDB-seeded Bearer sessions. 33/36 checks passed. Critical bug: /api/wedding/activate returns 500 on successful partner1 & partner2 activation paths — data is persisted but response serialization fails because the inserted `member_doc` retains a MongoDB `_id` (ObjectId) which is not JSON-serializable. Idempotency call succeeds because it uses find_one({}, {'_id':0}). This blocks the happy path from the frontend even though DB state is correct.
passed: GET /api/auth/me returns 401 without session and 200 with Bearer
POST /api/admin/tokens/generate via admin user creates WDL-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX (regex validated), non-admin blocked 403
Token activation: invalid format -> 400, unknown code -> 404, token normalization (lowercase input) accepted
Idempotency: same user re-activating returns reused=true with same wedding_id (200)
Third-user activation returns 409 with friendly message
PATCH /api/wedding partial saves; setup_complete seeds 20 checklist tasks; re-calling is idempotent (no duplicates)
GET /api/dashboard returns progress, days_to_go, this_week, budget, guests, vendors, upcoming
Budget CRUD, negative amounts rejected 400, totals correct
Guests CRUD, counts correct after RSVP update
User without wedding gets 403 on /checklist (multi-tenancy guard)

failed.issue: Returns 500 Internal Server Error although the wedding + membership are created in MongoDB. Backend log: ValueError: [TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable"), TypeError('vars() argument must have __dict__ attribute')]. Root cause: server.py inserts `member_doc` via insert_one which mutates the dict adding `_id: ObjectId(...)`. `wed_doc.pop('_id', None)` is called but `member_doc` is returned still containing the ObjectId, so FastAPI JSON encoding fails.
failed.evidence: curl POST /api/wedding/activate with WDL-DEMO-2026-LOVE as user A -> 500. Next call as same user returns 200 with reused=true proving DB write succeeded.

failed.issue: Same ObjectId serialization crash: 500 returned even though partner 2 membership row is created (third-user attempt correctly gets 409, confirming member_count reached 2).
failed.evidence: User B activation -> 500; subsequent user C attempt -> 409 'already connected to two accounts'.

failed.issue: These two checks could not be executed because the partner1 500 aborted the downstream test flow (no valid session had access to a wedding via a *successful* activation response). Backend logic itself likely works — the underlying membership was created — but retest is required after the activation serializer fix.
